jurisdiction.name: Yemen
jurisdiction.overview: No national AI law, strategy or AI-relevant data protection law has been published; regional records (UNESCO) appear separately.

narrative.summary: Yemen has no published AI-specific law, national AI strategy, AI ethics framework or AI governance body, and no official AI policy document could be located from either the internationally recognised government (Presidential Leadership Council and Cabinet, based in Aden) or the de facto authorities in Sana'a. There is also no comprehensive personal data protection law; privacy rests on constitutional and penal provisions that are not AI-specific. The Ministry of Telecommunications and Information Technology is the lead body for digital policy and, according to a UN ESCWA consultancy notice of May 2026, has asked ESCWA to support drafting a personal data protection law; no draft text is public. The Central Bank of Yemen (Aden) publishes banking circulars and laws online, none of which address AI. Yemen's AI-governance landscape is therefore at a pre-policy stage, shaped by conflict, a split administration and limited official web publishing; UNESCO's Recommendation on the Ethics of AI applies through the regional record.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Telecommunications and Information Technology
narrative.review_notes: Deep review completed on 7 October 2026. No national AI instruments were found, and all 18 categories are closed as searched with nothing found. Most ministry, cabinet, parliament and gazette websites could not be read, and part of the national web domain is administered from Sana'a, which makes it harder to tell which authority published a page. The Central Bank of Yemen's laws and circulars were read in full and contain nothing on AI. A personal data protection law and a draft law on electronic crimes are pending until official texts are found.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: All 18 categories searched in Arabic and English (2026-10-07); no official AI-relevant instrument from the Aden government or the Sana'a de facto authorities was located. Two unpublished items are held under leads. Technical review notes: Deep review 2026-10-07. No national instruments found; file closed with all 18 categories as searched/no material. Most .gov.ye sites (mtit.gov.ye, yemen.gov.ye, pmo.gov.ye, yemenparliament.gov.ye, nic.gov.ye) reset connections to automated access, and mopic.gov.ye and presidentyemen.org returned proxy 502 errors, so ministry, cabinet, parliament and gazette pages could not be browsed directly; the .ye domain space is also partly administered from Sana'a, which complicates attribution. cby-ye.com (Central Bank, Aden HQ) was read in full: laws list (central bank, banks, exchange, public debt, Islamic banks, AML/CFT, deposit insurance) and both pages of circulars contain nothing on AI. A Ministry of Justice journal article (almjalh.moj.gov.ye) on obstacles to using AI against cybercrime is academic research, not a policy instrument, and was excluded; it recommends adopting a pending draft law on electronic information crimes with AI provisions, but no official draft text was located. Commercial 'AI regulation in Yemen' explainers (levellers.ai, licentium.io etc.) were used only to confirm the absence finding, never as sources. No documents from the Sana'a de facto authorities on AI were located. Regional: Yemen is listed only in data/regional/UNESCO.json.

leads.note: A UN ESCWA consultancy notice (posted May 2026) states the Ministry asked ESCWA for advisory support to develop a personal data protection law for Yemen. No draft or consultation text is published on an official site. Record as a draft (data-privacy/drafts) once an official text appears.
